html:
SMTO-EML-0031 — The mail server refused the sign-in without saying why

GUID: 51d93dab-f4e5-5e27-be55-a4a12e7cf462
Slug: email-smtp-auth-exchange-rejected
Domain: EML · Subsystem: email-smtp

What happened

  • The mail server stopped the sign-in, but its reply doesn't say your password is wrong or explain the reason. SMTO stopped before sending this email.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Select Copy error details in this panel; the details include the mail server's reply code. The code tells your email administrator which server rule stopped the sign-in.
  2. Send those details to your email administrator and ask what the code means for your account. SMTO can't tell from this reply whether the cause is your account, a server rule or a server problem.
  3. Before asking SMTO to send again, check your Sent folder or ask a recipient whether the email already arrived. If an earlier attempt got through, sending again would create a duplicate.
  4. After the administrator fixes the cause, ask SMTO to test the connection, and send only if the email hasn't arrived. Testing first proves the sign-in works without sending real mail.

What success looks like

  • The connection test reports success, and the email reaches its recipients once.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details to your email administrator or the person who manages SMTO. Don't change your password or keep retrying; this reply doesn't show that the password is wrong.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • SMTP AUTH returned an unsuccessful reply other than 535, 454, 432, 534 or 538; the recorded reply does not establish invalid credentials.

What this means

  • The SMTP authentication exchange did not succeed; the recorded reply does not establish invalid credentials. Classification uses the SMTP reply or negotiated capability, never the server response prose.

Why this can happen

  • AUTH returns another unsuccessful reply without an established credential-specific cause.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the retained operation, condition and effect evidence before choosing a recovery action.

How to fix it

  • Read smtp_response_code from the result and review it with the mail administrator alongside the configured mechanism and mailbox policy. Fix the established protocol or policy cause, confirm with email.test_connection, and check existing send receipts before any new send attempt.
  • Inspect the SMTP reply code and authentication mechanism with the mail administrator. Correct the established protocol or policy issue before testing again.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the reported condition first; existing effect evidence and replay checks still decide whether a new attempt is permitted.

How to verify the fix

  • The reported prerequisite is satisfied and a new authorized operation returns its actual result.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a write whose external effect is still unknown.

Technical notes

  • Diagnostic presentation does not start recovery or alter authorization.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
